args.summary: The party met tide-reader Sela Thorn, explored the flooded Saltmere Mine and found a hymn page marked "M. Brand", watched the drowned bell ring above pale underwater shapes, and ended at the Tarred Gull planning a daylight chapel dive. The hidden Hollow Choir clock reached three of six.

properties.role: Tide-reader and boatwoman at Gullwick's pier four
properties.played_as: Whispers as though the water might hear her; avoids eye contact and watches the tide line. Grey braid and salt-stained coat; mends a net on an upturned skiff.
properties.wants: Will row the party for two silver, but never at night; offers to meet at pier four tomorrow at first light.

sources.quote: Sela Thorn. I read the tides. I'll row you, but not at night. Never at night.
She talks in a whisper, like the water might hear her, and she never once looks you in the eye. She keeps her gaze on the tide line.
There's a woman sitting on an upturned skiff, mending a net. Grey braid, salt-stained coat. She doesn't look up.
Fine, she'll do it for two silver.
Sela, Sella, the dockhands say it both ways.
She shrugs and goes back to her net. She says she'll be at pier four tomorrow at first light if you want the ride.

changes.why: Records the voiced boatwoman, her aliases, portrayal, and offered passage.

sources.quote: Morning in Gullwick. The fog is still sitting on the docks, gulls everywhere, and you're standing at the end of pier four looking for a boat.
There's a woman sitting on an upturned skiff, mending a net. Grey braid, salt-stained coat. She doesn't look up.

changes.why: Locates the party's meeting with Sela.

properties.statement: Sela says Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang, forty years ago; her grandmother said the rising water was warm.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: Preserves Sela's account and its secondhand origin without confirming the historical timing.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: Links the flooding account to the existing mine.

properties.details_shown: Up the cliff path, closed for forty years. Black entrance in chalk with half-rotted timbers and an overturned rusted cart. Warm air smells of old candle wax; wet hymn-book pages float on the water and cling to the walls.
properties.state: Closed; tunnel flooded with warm black water about thirty paces inside.

sources.quote: The Saltmere Mine entrance is a black mouth in the chalk, timber frame half rotted. A rusted cart lies on its side. The air coming out of it is warm and smells like a church, like old candle wax.
About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch. Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.

changes.why: Adds the observed mine condition while preserving its established closure.

change.name: The Saltmere hymn page marked M. Brand

properties.statement: A hymn-book page recovered at Saltmere Mine describes the sea giving back what it takes and bears the pencilled inscription "M. Brand".

sources.quote: I fish one out. What's on it?
A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".

changes.why: Records the physical clue without identifying its writer.

sources.quote: About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch. Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.
A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".

changes.why: Records where the clue was found.

properties.what_changed: Mira heard the bell the night she left. At Saltmere Mine, Teo found a hymn page marked "M. Brand" and identified the handwriting as his sister's, concluding she had been there. Her authorship and presence remain Teo's interpretation.

sources.quote: A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".
That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.

changes.why: Advances Teo's existing goal with the clue and his stated interpretation.

change.name: Is Maren involved with the choir?

properties.what_is_open: Vessa suspects Maren is in a cult and Oren suspects she runs the choir; neither claim has been confirmed.

sources.quote: Okay, I bet the harbor-master is behind all this. Maren wanted us gone from day one. She's in the cult, I'm calling it.
Yeah, Maren is totally running the choir.
You can think that. Roll investigation if you want to search the rest.

changes.why: Keeps the party's accusation as an unanswered thread rather than an NPC fact.

sources.quote: Yeah, Maren is totally running the choir.

changes.why: Identifies the subject of the party's suspicion.

properties.details_shown: Sank into the bay with its bell. At low water the roof protrudes, with the bell tower and two broken arches; seaweed hangs from the stones. At midnight pale shapes appear in rows on the submerged chapel floor, like a congregation, and vanish when the bell stops.

sources.quote: The drowned chapel's roof sticks out of the bay at low water, just the bell tower and two broken arches. Seaweed hangs from the stones.
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.

changes.why: Adds what the party actually saw without identifying the shapes.

properties.statement: Local fishermen say the Kelp Mother pulls children standing too close to the water under by their ankles; her existence is unconfirmed.

sources.quote: Don't stand that close. The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.
That's what the fishermen say. They pull their boat up and leave.

changes.why: Stores local folklore as rumor rather than creating a confirmed creature.

sources.quote: You get back to Gullwick by dusk, and you decide to go down to the shore below the old chapel ruins anyway, Sela's warning or not.
Don't stand that close. The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.

changes.why: Records where the warning was heard.

sources.quote: That's the choir clock at three of six.

changes.why: Applies the GM's explicit clock value; it remains hidden from players.

properties.what_is_open: Who or what rings the drowned bell? It rang twelve times again at midnight with louder humming; pale shapes stood in rows on the chapel floor and vanished when it stopped.

sources.quote: And then, right at midnight, the bell rings again under the water. Twelve times. And the humming is back, but louder. Much louder than two nights ago. You can feel it in your teeth.
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.

changes.why: Advances the existing bell mystery with observed evidence.

properties.next_step: The party plans to meet Sela at first light tomorrow, take her boat to the chapel, and dive at low tide during daylight. Vessa plans to buy rope and a second lantern tonight; neither purchases nor the dive have occurred on record.

sources.quote: At low tide, during the day. Not at night, Sela was right about that.
So tomorrow, first light, Sela rows us out and we dive to the chapel at low tide. I'll buy rope and a second lantern tonight.
Agreed. Tomorrow we dive.

changes.why: Records the party's agreed next step as a plan.

properties.what_changed: Mira heard the bell the night she left. Teo found a Saltmere hymn page marked "M. Brand" and identified the handwriting as Mira's, concluding she had been there. He believes the hymns came from the chapel and intends to follow the clue with tomorrow's daylight dive. These conclusions and the dive remain his interpretation and the party's plan.

sources.quote: Okay, plan. Mira wrote in that hymn book. The chapel is where the hymns came from. We go down to the chapel.
Agreed. Tomorrow we dive.

changes.why: Adds Teo's intended pursuit of the clue without establishing the hymn's origin.

properties.details_shown: Tavern by the Gullwick docks, with a fire and the smell of tar and fish stew.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.

changes.why: Records the place where the session ended.

properties.played_as: Huge, red-bearded; laughs at his own jokes and wipes the same mug throughout the conversation. Teases the party as brave or stupid and gives them stew on the house.

sources.quote: The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.
You lot went to the shore at midnight? Brave or stupid. On the house, either way.
Bram is huge, red beard, laughs at his own jokes, and he wipes the same mug the whole time he talks to you.

changes.why: Records the voiced innkeeper and his portrayal.

properties.knows: Says he has known Maren for thirty years, calls her sharp-tongued with a good heart, and says she lost a brother to the bay.

sources.quote: Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: Preserves Bram's account as his claim.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.
The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.

changes.why: Records where Bram works.

sources.quote: The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.

changes.why: Records Bram's latest appearance.

change.name: Bram's account of Maren's lost brother

properties.statement: Bram says Maren lost a brother to the bay and describes her as having a sharp tongue and a good heart; this is his testimony.

sources.quote: Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: Records relevant testimony without assigning unconfirmed history directly to Maren.

sources.quote: Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: Links the testimony to its subject or speaker.

sources.quote: Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: Links the testimony to its subject or speaker.

properties.what_is_open: Vessa suspects Maren is in a cult and Oren suspects she runs the choir, without confirmation. Bram subsequently says she has a good heart and lost a brother to the bay; his testimony does not settle the suspicion.

sources.quote: Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: Adds the later testimony to the open suspicion without resolving it.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.
Yes, long rest, you're all back to full. And that's where we stop for tonight.

changes.why: Records the character's location at the end of the session.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.
Yes, long rest, you're all back to full. And that's where we stop for tonight.

changes.why: Records the character's location at the end of the session.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.
Yes, long rest, you're all back to full. And that's where we stop for tonight.

changes.why: Records the character's location at the end of the session.

properties.knows: Claims hers is the only boat that goes near the bell water because the others are scared. Says Saltmere flooded when the bell first rang forty years ago; her grandmother said the water rose warm.

sources.quote: Sella's boat is the only one that goes near the bell water. The others are scared.
Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: Records Sela's stated knowledge with the claims and secondhand account attributed.

properties.role: One of two fishermen hauling a boat ashore below the old chapel
properties.played_as: Warns the party not to stand close to the water; says the Kelp Mother pulls children down by their ankles and insists "Everyone knows that." Hauls the boat up with his companion and leaves.

sources.quote: Two fishermen hauling their boat up. One of them sees you looking at the water.
Don't stand that close. The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.
That's what the fishermen say. They pull their boat up and leave.

changes.why: Preserves the unnamed voiced NPC using only his recorded speech and actions.
